note: The colonial name for Khoekhoe people. It is now widely regarded as offensive. Translations keep it where the diarists used it, because the translation reproduces their words. Editorial notes, README text and anything written in our own voice use Khoekhoe (or Khoe, or the name of a specific people) and never this word.

The diarists' word for Xhosa people and their country. In South Africa the word later became a severe racial slur. Translations keep it where the diarists used it, and a note on first use explains it. Our own writing uses Xhosa. The normalised column sometimes replaces it with 'Xhosa' (A363597 line 2098); translations follow the diplomatic transcription.
Dutch and Afrikaans for master or boss; used by a Khoekhoe speaker addressing a farmer.
